html:
The Putumayo genocide was the enslavement and mass killing of Indigenous peoples in the Putumayo region of the north-west Amazon during the Amazon rubber boom, worst in the early 1900s.

The Peruvian rubber baron Julio César Arana took control of the land, disputed between Peru and Colombia, and in 1907 registered his firm in London as the Peruvian Amazon Company. Its agents forced the Huitoto, Bora, Andoque, Ocaina, Miraña, Resígaro and others to collect wild rubber through flogging, mutilation and killing. Tens of thousands died.

Reports from 1909, and the 1912 report of the British consul Roger Casement, who had earlier exposed Congo rubber, caused a scandal, and the company collapsed. Arana was never punished.
sum: The Putumayo genocide was the enslavement and mass killing of Indigenous peoples in the Putumayo region of the north-west Amazon during the Amazon rubber boom, worst in the early 1900s.
